scope: Sequential authenticated synthetic UI lab on local Windows host; no model inference during measurements
command: npm.cmd run build; npm.cmd run benchmark:ui
conditions: Three cold and three warm navigations per profile. Per-Store disposable fixture and private cookie authentication. CPU profile collected separately after repetitions. 40messages/20long responses. Four labels preserve exploratory, revised baseline, initial candidate and final verified data.
decision: Keep native offscreen layout for older messages only, with explicit keyboard reading protection. Final phone warm median1131.8ms versus1452.3ms baseline (22.1percent); all preserved behavior gates pass.
verification: Full affected22browser cases pass2.9min, then final focus refinement3cases21.2s; fresh strict build/final types and final12navigation measurements pass.
limitations: Phone-layout uses a desktop Chromium viewport,4xCPU and synthetic80ms/10Mbps/2Mbps network; not calibrated physical Galaxy/Android/Samsung Internet.
Readiness and keyboard-to-two-frame values are laboratory proxies, not field INP, display-paint time or model latency.
History driver-inclusive timing includes automation overhead; actual click-to-two-frame timing was added in baseline-v2.

Initial candidate failed old-code focus and a landscape test setup whose native anchoring prevented its intended gap. Focus behavior repaired; landscape fixture disables native anchoring while retaining all assertions.
Small sequential sample sets on one host, not population guarantees; screen-reader and physical-phone acceptance remains open.
Latest two messages remain normally rendered; all content remains in the DOM. No virtual-list library or new runtime dependency.
